🇷🇺
🎙
Interview of the Russian Ambassador to the Netherlands, H.E. V.Tarabrin, with Dutch blogger R.Brouwer
Key points:
🔹
On the UN.
Despite growing confrontation and the increasing politicization of international relations, the UN remains one of the few universal platforms for discussing global challenges and seeking solutions to them. This is precisely why the Organization continues to be of exceptional importance.
🔹
On the new world map.
Russia has supported “Correct the Map” resolution of the UN General Assembly. We regard its adoption as a fair attempt to promote a diversity of approaches and ensure a more objective representation of the world’s regions.
🔹
On UN Security Council reform.
Russia advocates broader representation of the countries of the Global Majority and supports the inclusion of India, Brazil and representatives of Africa in the UN Security Council. At the same time, we oppose granting such status to Germany and Japan, as the Western group is already disproportionately represented in the Security Council.
🔹
On the objectives of the Special Military Operation.
Russia seeks to ensure that Ukraine ceases to be an aggressive anti-Russian project and no longer poses a military threat to Russia or its neighbours. Our stated objectives also include Ukraine’s neutral status, the restoration of the rights of the Russian language, Russian culture and the Russian Orthodox Church as well as recognition of the existing territorial realities on the ground and the will expressed by the residents of the Donetsk and Lugansk People’s Republics and the Zaporozhye and Kherson Regions.
🔹
On Russia-US contacts.
Visits by US representatives to Moscow provide a useful channel for mediation diplomacy and make it possible to seek areas of common ground. At the same time, the main obstacle to a peaceful settlement remains the position of the European Union, which continues to pursue the goal of inflicting a “strategic defeat” on Russia.
🔹
On the drone incident in Leipzig.
We categorically reject allegations of Russian involvement in the drone incident. No evidence substantiating such claims has been presented. Nevertheless, the incident was used as a pretext for further anti-Russian measures by Germany.
🔹
On relations with NATO.
Under M.Rutte, relations between Russia and the Alliance have continued to deteriorate. We regard aggressive anti-Russian rhetoric and the build-up of military activity along Russia’s borders as signs of NATO preparing for a possible conflict with Russia and consider this trend extremely dangerous.
🔹
On relations with the Netherlands.
Bilateral ties are at an extremely low point. The Hague has effectively placed itself at the forefront of the anti-Russian camp, actively contributing to militarization and pursuing a confrontational course. At the same time, rising military expenditure means that enormous resources that could otherwise be directed towards social welfare, healthcare, education and transport are instead being spent on armaments and further fuelling the spiral of confrontation with Russia.
🔹
On the threat of a direct confrontation with Europe.
Russia is not interested in a war with European countries and has no aggressive plans towards Europe. However, the current course pursued by European countries is becoming increasingly dangerous. A direct military confrontation between Russia and Europe risks rapidly escalating into a nuclear conflict with devastating consequences.

item.title: . #Announcement On October 2-26, 2026, media representatives and bloggers can apply for accreditation
item.description: #Announcement On October 2-26, 2026, media representatives and bloggers can apply for accreditation to cover the “Peoples of Russia” International Week . ℹ️ The “Peoples of Russia” International Week is held annually pursuant to Presidential Executive Order No. 382 of June 1, 2026, declaring 2026 the Year of Unity of the Peoples of Russia . Its central theme is “Solidarity among States through the Unity of Peoples and Traditional Values” . The events are coordinated by the Executive Office of the Security Council of the Russian Federation and organised by the Roscongress Foundation . Russian and foreign media outlets, as well as bloggers, may apply in accordance with the accreditation rules published in the “Media” section of the Week’s official website . 📄 Programme Overview of the “Peoples of Russia” International Week Stay tuned for updates on the official website and via email newsletters. ✉️ For media accreditation enquiries, please contact: media@roscongress.org

item.title: 🗓 On October 5, Moscow hosted the eighth meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
item.description: 🗓 On October 5, Moscow hosted the eighth meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan , attended by special representatives and senior officials from Russia, Afghanistan, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, China, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan . Afghanistan’s delegation was led by Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi . Delegations from Belarus and Egypt attended as guests. 👉 Sergey Lavrov’s remarks at the eighth meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan *** The Moscow Format Consultations provide an authoritative multilateral platform for countries in the region to coordinate practical approaches to issues related to Afghanistan. During the meeting, participants reaffirmed that there is no alternative to developing cooperation with Kabul on an equal and mutually beneficial basis and supporting Afghanistan’s integration into the global economy. Participants once again called on the international community to provide regular humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people , stressing that such aid must not be politicised . 🤝 On the sidelines of the event, Sergey Lavrov held separate talks with Foreign Minister of Afghanistan Amir Khan Muttaqi . The Ministers discussed prospects for developing bilateral cooperation and working together in international and regional forums.

August 2026 marked the fifth anniversary of Afghanistan’s liberation from
two decades of Western occupation
. The vast military machine of the US and its NATO allies crumbled in the face of the Afghan people’s fighting spirit and determination, forcing the occupiers to flee. A national government led by the Taliban movement came to power and established control over the country. I
t must be acknowledged that it has governed with a fair degree of success.
Afghan security forces are waging an uncompromising fight against ISIS and other terrorist groups
. Hundreds of militants have been eliminated, and a number of high-profile terrorist attacks, including those targeting foreign nationals and diplomatic missions, have been foiled. Importantly, helping strengthen Kabul’s counterterrorism capabilities by providing material and expert assistance and maintaining contacts between intelligence and law enforcement agencies
meets the interests of all of us
.
The measures the Afghan government is taking to combat illicit drug trafficking produce results
. According to expert assessments by
the UN Office on Drugs and Crime
, opiate production in that country
has declined by 90%
since 2022.
The Afghan economy continues to grow despite the tough sanctions imposed by Western countries
, which, under the pretext of protecting human rights, have cut the Islamic Emirate off from the international financial system and seized its national banking assets. This is what the West is practicing on a regular basis.
Unfortunately, the humanitarian situation in the country remains difficult
.
According to the UN
,
more than 17 million Afghans
- nearly half the population -
will face food shortages this coming winter
, and the total number of people in need of humanitarian aid will reach
22 million
. Clearly, relevant international agencies need to step up, and bilateral efforts need to be deployed to address the situation at hand.
Russia will continue to provide regular humanitarian aid
, and
another batch
will arrive in Afghanistan in the coming months.
❗️
The deployment of NATO military infrastructure in Afghanistan and neighbouring countries under any pretext whatsoever is categorically unacceptable
. As we know from history, presence of this kind carries the risk of destabilisation and heightened tensions and conflict. We have seen no other outcome from this kind of presence over the past several decades.
I am confident that your meeting will be
constructive
and contribute to
Afghanistan’s further development as an independent and sustainable state
, and help promote peace and stability throughout the region.

item.description: ⚡️ Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation : Following an application by the Prosecutor General’s Office of the Russian Federation, Baltic nationalists have been recognised by a court as accomplices of Nazi Germany in war crimes and crimes against humanity committed against the Soviet people during the Great Patriotic War – a finding of legal significance. Recognition of this fact is not only an evident conclusion stemming from the principal legal findings of the Nuremberg Trials , but also a historical duty that society and the state owe to those who fought in the war, its veterans and its victims . ⚖️ It has been established that the Nazi invaders committed atrocities with the direct involvement of their accomplices – Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian nationalists ( 13 individuals and five organisations ). According to records from the archives of Russia’s Federal Security Service , Foreign Ministry and Defence Ministry , as well as the State Archive of the Russian Federation , following Germany’s attack on the USSR , the Nazis recruited Baltic nationalists from among local residents to do their “dirty work” in the occupied territories . They carried out punitive operations against civilians and Soviet POWs. Through their actions, the territories of the Baltic countries – Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia – became killing grounds during the Great Patriotic War for POWs, Soviet officials and their families, and people suspected of sympathising with the Red Army. ▪️

item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : PHOTO FACTS & EVIDENCE of crimes committed by Ukrainian armed forces over the week of September 28 – October 4, 2026 : ▪️ September 28 – balloons carrying propaganda leaflets, a radio repeater and Lepestok anti-personnel mines were shot down over the Belgorod Region. ▪️ September 28 – a UAV strike on an apartment building in Voronezh, Voronezh Region. The overnight UAV raid on the city’s residential neighbourhoods resulted in injuries to 13 civilians. ▪️ September 30 – a UAV strike on a grocery store in Novaya Kakhovka, Kherson Region. ▪️ September 30 – a UAV strike on a civilian car in the village of Raiskoye, Kherson Region. ▪️ October 2 – a UAV strike on an EMERCOM vehicle in Donetsk, DPR.
